title: ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 NVIDIA HGX B300 8-GPU Server Review
gist: ASRock Rack's 4U16X-GNR2 packs dual Intel Xeon 6 'Granite Rapids' CPUs and 8 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs (HGX B300) into a liquid-cooled 4U chassis with front-panel 6.4Tbps networking, offered in either direct-liquid-cooled or ZutaCore two-phase versions; ServeTheHome discloses the review was sponsored by ASRock Rack.

insights.claim: ASRock Rack's 4U16X-GNR2 combines two Intel Xeon 6 'Granite Rapids' CPUs with eight NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs (NVIDIA HGX B300 platform) and onboard NVLink interconnect in a single 4U liquid-cooled chassis.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Signals continued vendor push to cram full 8-GPU HGX B300 nodes into smaller, liquid-cooled 4U footprints, a config an investor can track as a density/efficiency benchmark for AI training/inference server suppliers competing with Nvidia's reference designs and larger OEMs.
insights.locator: The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is a large NVIDIA HGX B300 system.

insights.claim: The author argues that although a 4U chassis sounds large, it is actually extremely dense relative to an air-cooled equivalent of the same 8-GPU HGX B300 configuration.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Reinforces the thesis that liquid cooling is becoming a prerequisite for maximizing GPU density per rack unit in next-gen AI clusters, relevant to data center capex and cooling-vendor demand.
insights.quote: Some may think that 4U is a large system, but it is extremely dense compared to an air-cooled version.

insights.claim: ASRock Rack sells the 4U16X-GNR2 in two liquid-cooled variants: a traditional direct-liquid-cooling (DLC) version and a ZutaCore two-phase cooling version for customers who want to avoid water in their loops.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Offering both DLC and two-phase ZutaCore options lets ASRock Rack address data centers with different risk tolerances for liquid-in-rack cooling, a differentiator worth tracking versus rivals standardizing on a single cooling method.
insights.quote: We also saw a ZutaCore-cooled model that day, which provides two-phase cooling for those who do not want water in their loops.
insights.locator: Full disclosure: We saw this and took photos in Taipei, Taiwan

insights.claim: The 4U16X-GNR2 includes eight OSFP 800Gbps cages on the front panel, delivering over 6.4Tbps of network bandwidth before any additional PCIe network card is installed.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Baseline 6.4Tbps of front-panel networking on an 8-GPU node highlights how much bandwidth AI training/inference clusters now require per server, a demand signal for optical/copper interconnect and switch-silicon suppliers.
insights.quote: Even without adding a PCIe card, this system has over 6.4Tbps of network bandwidth on this front panel alone.
insights.locator: Next to those ports are the CPU liquid-cooling hose inlet and outlet.

insights.claim: The server's management port and two 1GbE (Intel i350-based) ports can be relocated between the front and rear of the chassis via internal cables, so operators can mix front/rear placement without needing a separate SKU.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A single-SKU cabling-flexibility design reduces inventory/configuration complexity for data center buyers, a small but real cost/logistics edge for ASRock Rack versus fixed-port competitors.
insights.quote: That is a simple solution that means one server version can handle many data center cabling needs without requiring a separate SKU.
insights.locator: If you want a combination of these, for example, to have the management port in the front and 1GbE ports in the rear

insights.claim: The system has 12x 2.5-inch U.2 NVMe bays on the front, with 2 bays connected directly to the CPU and the remaining 10 connected to the PCIe switch complex.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Splitting NVMe bays between CPU-attached and PCIe-switch-attached paths lets operators separate boot/OS storage from high-throughput GPU-adjacent storage, relevant to how AI server vendors architect local caching for training data.
insights.locator: There are 12x 2.5″ U.2 NVMe bays on the front of the system.

insights.claim: The 4U16X-GNR2 uses ten 3kW 80Plus Titanium power supplies in the rear to provide redundancy for the 8-GPU HGX B300 configuration.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Ten 3kW Titanium-rated PSUs (up to 30kW capacity) underscore the extreme power density of 8-GPU Blackwell Ultra nodes, a data point for estimating power infrastructure and PSU-market demand tied to AI server buildouts.
insights.locator: Ten 3kW 80Plus Titanium CPUs are in the rear of the system to provide redundancy.

insights.claim: ServeTheHome discloses that its hands-on look at the 4U16X-GNR2, including photos taken in Taipei and follow-up remote access, was arranged by ASRock Rack, making the review sponsored.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Sponsorship disclosure means claims about the product should be weighted as vendor-influenced marketing content rather than fully independent benchmarking, tempering how much investor signal to extract from performance framing.
insights.quote: Full disclosure: We saw this and took photos in Taipei, Taiwan, during a trip earlier this year, and then ASRock Rack set us up with remote access, so we have to say this is sponsored.
insights.locator: Full disclosure: We saw this and took photos in Taipei, Taiwan
